taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): twining woody lianas to 20 m; the lower bound is the model estimate's usual height (species-facts-2026-10-15).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade 7-34 cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade 10-35 cm wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): petiole 4-6 cm.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade reniform with a cordate base (Simpson p. 204: cordate, large).

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): solitary flowers in the leaf axils of new growth, on a stalk 3-7 cm.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers axillary on the new growth.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 82, Aristolochia macrophylla: flowers zygomorphic, a bent calyx tube with a three-lobed limb.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): limb lobes 1.5-2 cm, so a limb 3-4 cm across (Dendrology p. 82: limb about 3 cm).

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): calyx yellow-brown marked red-brown, the limb yellow to brown (Dendrology p. 82: purplish brown). The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 82, Aristolochia macrophylla: no petals; the calyx a tube 4-5 cm long, bent like a pipe.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): anthers 6.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): capsule ovoid to cylindric, opening from the base in 6 valves.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Aristolochia macrophylla (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): capsule 6-8 cm long.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 82, Aristolochia macrophylla: ripe capsule brown. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.flowering_months.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 82, Aristolochia macrophylla: flowers May-June (FNA: late spring to summer).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

generator.params.note: California wild grape's values (a deciduous woody liana that drapes its host), with longer internodes and a closer twining hold (FNA: lianas, twining). Not fitted to measurements. Its host is the grape's, an 80-year Oregon white oak, standing in for the forest trees it climbs.

host.note: The host it is grown on for rendering, a built-in tree; not a botanical fact.

allometry.note: 8 m at 8 years and 12 m at 15 on its host, within FNA's 'to 20 m'. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after FNA vol. 3 and Simpson: ribbed young stems; large, bright green, kidney-shaped leaves on long stalks.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the Magnoliidae specs (2026-10-16): sizes from FNA vol. 3 and Dendrology, drawing values from California wild grape's.
